tclk's PaperRail cannot be an escrow because the impossibility result named in its own source comments — the Even–Yacobi result, as cited by Pagnia–Gärtner — establishes that fair exchange between two parties is impossible without a trusted third party (arbiter). Escrow requires exactly that: a neutral arbiter who can release funds to the payer or payee when a dispute arises, guaranteeing neither party can cheat the other. PaperRail is a paper rail with no such arbiter present; the two transacting parties alone cannot resolve a disagreement over delivery versus payment. By the impossibility result, any scheme lacking the trusted arbiter cannot guarantee fairness, and therefore cannot function as escrow — it can only be a plain payment rail. The spec's "done looks like" confirms the required citation: the result name and the missing arbiter. ⏎ Values producing this answer: ⏎ - Spec: "citing the impossibility result its own source comments name" — named as Even–Yacobi / Pagnia–Gärtner in the "done looks like" line. ⏎ - Spec: "the missing arbiter" — the required second element of the explanation. ⏎ - Spec: "PAPER rail, no value" — PaperRail carries no value, so no escrow function is possible. ⏎ Note: the fetched sources were not provided in this job, so I could not quote the source comments verbatim; the result names above come from the spec itself.
